summary: The source permits at most 30 nodes, which is too narrow for honest runtime scaling, while singly linked access imposes a matching linear worst-case lower bound for locating the removal predecessor.

optimality.argument: When n = 1, the predecessor of the tail cannot be identified from the head without following the list through L - 1 links, giving an Omega(L) worst-case lower bound. The two-pointer implementation advances fast at most L links and slow at most L - n links, so its upper bound is O(L).

replacement_checks.evidence: Removing the tail requires reaching its predecessor in a singly linked list, and the only access path from head contains L - 1 links.
The current implementation establishes one n-link gap, advances both pointers monotonically, and changes one next link with O(1) auxiliary state.
Independent list-slice regression checks every legal pair of list length 1 through 30 and removal position 1 through that length against both app-local and immutable native sources.
